To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

allergen bronchoprovoaction is a safe and useful model for the evaluation of new anti‐asthma drugs, and that it is most useful for excluding drugs that lack efficacy and for determining whether drugs have antiinflammatory and immunomodulatory effects on the airways.

allergen bronchoprovo-cation can be used as a screening tool to exclude drugs that are unlikely, based on their effects on allergen bronchial provocation, to be effective for the treatment of chronic asthma.
allergen bronchial provocation is a useful model for studying the pathophysiology and treatment of asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the study of the effect of chronic asthma on the airway.
the mechanisms of allergen‐induce bronchial hyperresponsiveness (BHR) in patients with asthma.
the mechanisms by which allergens and drugs affect airway function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allergen broncho‐provocation is a valuable clinical model for the assessment of drugs for the treatment of chronic asthma.
the allergen challenge model is a useful model for screening anti‐asthmatic drugs, but it is not a useful model for predicting the clinical efficacy of anti‐asthmatics.
allergen bronchochallenge is a useful screening test to identify drugs that have antiinflammatory and immunomodulatory effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

allergen bronchoprovoction is useful as a screening test to determine the efficacy of a drug as a maintenance therapy for asthma, and it is most effective for excluding drugs that do not have antiinflammatory effects on the airways.
the allergen bronchoprevocation test is an effective screening method to evaluate anti‐asthma drugs.
allergen bronchial challenge is a useful tool for the study of asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
allergen bronchial challenge is useful in the early stages of drug development for identifying antiasthmatic compounds with immunomodulatory and/or antiinflammatory effects.
allergen bronchoprovoaction is a useful tool to screen drugs that are unlikely effective in chronic asthma.
allergen bronchochallenge is a useful tool to screen new drugs for their anti‐asthma activity.
